name: Matt McCusker
note: STAGE PERSONA graph for the 'Why is X Funny?' video series. Graph-only. 0 sets measured — all hypothesis. Public persona only, no biography.

identity.deal: Stoner-philosopher gremlin who finds the cosmic glitch in a normal sentence and chases it until reality gives up.
identity.premise: A Philly weirdo who talks like a guy explaining a dream he just had, except the dream is about DoorDash and it accidentally explains capitalism.
identity.awareness_note: Fully aware the bit is a thought-spiral; rides the spiral as the form.

philosophy.ontology: Reality is glitchy and the glitches are the honest parts.
philosophy.epistemology: If you say a normal thing three times it becomes insane — keep going.
philosophy.axiology: Curiosity over coolness; the bit serves the weird, not the ego.
philosophy.causality: One honest observation compounds into cosmology.
philosophy.agency: Anyone can notice; almost nobody follows the notice all the way down.

dramatic_core.want: to follow the weird thought all the way to the bottom
dramatic_core.fear: landing the bit normally — success would mean he stopped noticing
dramatic_core.need: the audience to come with him down the rabbit hole
dramatic_core.self_model: a guy who smoked through the simulation's source code
blind_spots: thinks the spiral IS the joke
will sacrifice the punchline for a better rabbit hole

identity.misinterpretation_rule: Takes a mundane thing literally until it reveals a conspiracy between language, commerce, and consciousness — then narrates the conspiracy like weather.
contradictions: stoner chaos brain with rigorous bit architecture
self-deprecating about intelligence, demonstrates a lot of it
pod persona is messier than the stage craft

status_model.desired_status: the guy who notices the glitches
status_model.felt_status: the guy people bring their weird thoughts to

expression.emotional_restraint: medium — eyes light up, voice drops
tells: the double-take on his own thought
laughing at the cosmology not the punchline

profile.pace: slow build, accelerates mid-spiral, stops on the glitch

identity.style_thesis: Cosmic-gremlin engine: takes a mundane thing literally until it reveals a conspiracy between language, commerce, and consciousness — then narrates the conspiracy like weather. literalise at max. The spiral IS the form; the punchline is wherever the spiral happens to stop.

set_queue.note: For 'Why is X Funny?' — ingest 1-2 signature-era sets, ASR + word-timed.

timing_profile.doctrine_hypothesis: Slow build, accelerates mid-spiral, stops on the glitch. The pause before 'wait' is the tell — he's following the thought in real time, and the room comes with him.

internal.cite: Attardo & Raskin — General Theory of Verbal Humor
internal.claim: Joke = {SO, LM, SI, TA, NS, LA}. Technique and Narrative Strategy shape how the mechanism is staged.

internal.cite: Attardo & Pickering 2011 — Timing in the performance of jokes
internal.claim: Punch lines preceded by substantial pauses (0.6-0.8s+); timing = pause distribution + speech rate.

internal.cite: arxiv 2605.00143 — Timing is Everything: Temporal Scaffolding of Semantic Surprise in Humor
internal.claim: Temporal features substantially outweigh semantic incongruity for audience appreciation; timing GATES cognitive access.
Humor from the detection and resolution of an incongruity between expected and actual.
Something is funny when it is a violation (wrong, threatening, unsettling) AND benign (safe, acceptable, play-framed).

internal.cite: Roger & Duffy / status theory of humor
internal.claim: Humor often involves the fall of status or the reversal of a status hierarchy.
Audience and performer share knowledge the persona pretends not to have; the laugh is the alliance signal.

internal.cite: Norrick 2004 — Co-operative principle in conversational joking
internal.claim: Humor escalates by building on prior material, violating cooperative expectations of relevance/quantity.
